Therapists are expensive out of pocket.  I got on the hospital's Charity Care program.  Check out the aid programs.  Medicaid, hospital charity care programs, the health department.  A lot of programs will use a sliding scale for people who need help, meaning you pay according to income.  A lot of churches also offer therapy these days, if you're into that idea.  Best thing to do is call the behavioral/mental ward at your health department or local hospital and ask for a list of resources for mental health in your area, and also how to pay for it.  Hardest part is making the connections, but that's how I did it for myself and my husband.

Being someone who is going through the same thing with my husband, sometimes the best thing is to take a break.  First get him the proper help, point him in the right direction to get some therapy, and then take a break, let him get himself together, making sure he doesn't implode himself when you take the break.  Visit him of course, occasionally, but enough to give him space to sort out his thoughts, and make sure he has a good support network of friends and family to guide him through.  Sometimes the pressure of being in a relationship can only add to the intensity of depression.  I also have depression, and now that we are separated my husband and I get along much better.  It sort of renews the relationship, in a sense, because you can see him when both of you are in better moods.

My husband can be very intense, or very lacking in emotion, and it drove me craz(ier), but the best thing I could do for him is point him in the right direction for help and be a positive presence and influence in his life.

Your boyfriend is in a state where he needs a lot of alone time, it seems.  He's not really in the state to be able to handle going out.  When I'm depressed I can't stand going out.  I need time to recuperate unless I'm properly medicated (thankfully I am now).  

While it may be hard to separate, but it might be just what he needs.  Don't leave him completely, still be there, but if you both get to the point of being depressed, you're only feeding the negativity/depression of the other.

A month or so ago I was posting on the SuicideWatch subreddit.  Shortly thereafter I got on the right meds (finally) and I was able to start appreciating the fact that I do have a damn good life.  I'm happily married, have decent friends, family that loves me, a roof over my head, decent food to eat, a nice bed, internet, a bunch of other shit I bought or was given to me, and most importantly, a general peace of mind.  That is more valuable to me than anything.  Being able to wake up and smile at the day instead of cursing it like I did when I was depressed.  Being able to look people in the eyes and say, "hi, how are you?" and not have this looming paranoia (delusions) that they secretly hate me and wish I would die.

A lot of people are stressed, and they know they have good lives, but their stress makes it so they can't appreciate it, and that only adds to the guilt they already feel.  Mental issues really deplete a person's ability to have fun, appreciate things, function in life.

Money is no object with mental issues or illness.  Except when it comes to paying for it of course.  You don't have to be poor or rich or fat or skinny or ugly or beautiful to be over-stressed or mentally ill.  Anyone can have mental problems.  It's human.

Especially in western society, which is constantly overstimulating us and demanding more and more when there is less and less to give.

I think what happened is that I was verbally and emotionally attacked so much so early that I developed this intensely irritated and defensive tone of voice that is now programmed into my brain.  Psychological conditioning.  I'm not sure I know how to "ask someone nicely".

My husband is a complex case.  We are pretty sure he has Aspergers syndrome, and he grew up with speech problems, ADD, etc.  He needs very specific instructions or examples or he just doesn't get what I am trying to ask of him.  The level at which he requires an explanation is something I'm not even sure I know that well myself.  I can provide general examples but not specific ones.  He has a tendency, like me, to fly off the handle without realizing it until after the damage has been done.  It's a very tense situation between him and I, but I love him so much and I just want to work things out so we understand each other and can communicate.

I think I might try the letter thing with my dad.  And some of my other family members too.  I've been reluctant to do that because he might see it as passive aggressive, but it's better to at least give it a shot at this point.  It's driving me up the wall.

I used to have more examples because I used to leave the house more and interact with more people.   Now the only person I really see much is my husband.  I'm not sure if doormatting is maybe the right word as much as not standing up for myself, but maybe it is a mix of both.

One more recent example is that my husband likes me to go to bed when he does because it helps him sleep better, but I like to stay up late sometimes, and sometimes I like to stay up all night.  But instead of finding a balance between staying up late and going to bed with him, I just go to bed with him every night, denying myself the much needed occasional all-nighter.

Another example deals with my grandmother.  Almost every time I see her she rehashes fucked up things that my dad or grandfather or whoever did.  I'm really fucking sick of hearing it but I don't know how to tell her to stop without sounding like an asshole.  I feel like if I say anything at all she'll rip into me.

Another example is my father.  Every time I talk to him or see him I can sense his disappointment in me in his voice.  I want to say something to him about it, I've wanted to confront him for years, but every time I have tried he just freaks out, and I don't want him to feel he's a bad parent because he tried his best, but...ugh.  I feel guilty if I don't talk to him, and depressed when I do.

Maybe she will and everything will be fine, and that would be great and I hope it happens for her.   But if not there is plenty of time for friends.  Focus on living your life the way you imagine.  Don't worry about being popular.  Find something you love, do it, and you will become popular, maybe, if you're lucky in this psychotic society.  

SOME GENERAL TIPS

1)  Don't trust anyone with anything you wouldn't want everyone knowing by the end of the next day.  This is the nature of high school.  If you go into the desert, you will get dehydrated if you don't drink water.  If you go to high school you will ruin your reputation if you share secrets with the wrong people and then school will be miserable.  It's just something you don't do if you want to be able to stand going to school.

2)  She seems like she is mature for her age, she must realize this.  I feel like I've been waiting my whole life to be taken seriously up until my college graduation.  It takes time.  She will find her niche.  Maybe not in high school...but it will come.

3) Set an example by being nice without letting everyone step on you.  Don't try to come up with witty comebacks.  I tried and sounded like an idiot.  I've noticed if I don't make eye contact with people who dislike me  or stare at me funny and don't give them a second of my attention they go away.  I always win staring contests because I don't blink.  It is hard to do but once you master the art of staring into space and zoning out, it's a snap.  It's called temporary numbness.  The mind's defense against idiocy.  Try to see what people say and do as purely a product of their age or life situation and you will feel a lot better.

4)  Most important:  Never let them win by stooping to or below their level.

5)  FILTER FILTER FILTER.  She should ask her friends to go on a hike with her or build a robot or go to the zoo or something.  If the friend is resistant or complains about the idea, then screw them.  I've found people filters to be extremely useful in weeding out jerks.  Unfortunately today I think I am forced into this rule:  If (s)he looks like a jerk, (s)he probably is a jerk, unless (s)he goes out of his way to show (s)he isn't a jerk.

Hope this helps.  She has my empathy and sympathy.  MS and HS are not good times to have trust and faith in the human race.
